decisions.reason: As a close extension of the pipeline component range, Product A showed the strongest continuation signal among the launches and likely met at least minimum aspiration levels, so we would retain it.

Although related to existing fabrication capabilities, Product B disappeared from the website quickly, suggesting results below aspiration and too little evidence to justify using scarce production and sales resources on it.
Product C fit the firm's skills but not its observed market traction, and its rapid disappearance indicates underperformance relative to aspiration compared with more promising core-line products.

Product D leveraged coating and metalworking capacity but was distant from the core water-infrastructure offer, and without continued market visibility it likely fell short of aspirations and should release resources for core uses.

Product E was also outside the main product-market focus, and the lack of sustained presence suggests the experiment did not perform well enough to merit retention under boundedly rational portfolio review.

Product F appears to have been a peripheral trial using existing fabrication resources, but with no sign of sustained acceptance it is better dropped so capacity can support the established business and nearer developments.
